title: Cost Structure and the Usefulness of Earnings
eligible_reason: No staggered binary design. The main analyses are cross-sectional earnings-response regressions (car/bhar/analyst-forecast dispersion on UE x DOL with UE x controls) with industry and year FE. The only DiD (Table 6) uses the granting of PNTR to China: continuous industry NTR gap (treated_pntr) x a common post indicator (post_pntr_bill = year > 2000), with industry and year FE (not firm FE), time-varying controls and robust SE; the event-study version interacts treated_pntr with time dummies (ib5.time). Single adoption date and continuous treatment intensity.
design_notes: analyses.dta (Compustat/CRSP/IBES-derived firm-year data shipped). Table 6 (DO_Analyses.do lines 142-148): reghdfe dol_lev/dol_ke/earnvol1_36 c.treated_pntr##c.post_pntr_bill + controls, absorb(ind year), years 1991-2011; ERC versions with c.quartsue##c.treated_pntr##c.post_pntr_bill. Figure (lines 168-170): c.treated_pntr##ib5.time. Table 7: forced CEO turnover on performance x DOL with firm and year FE (continuous interactions).
estimators_reported: OLS/reghdfe with industry and year FE (cross-sectional ERC)
main_or_robustness: PNTR DiD is a supplementary test (Table 6); main analyses cross-sectional
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Common post date (after 2000, PNTR); treatment is the continuous NTR gap.

specs.exclusion_reason: single common treatment date (post 2000); continuous treatment intensity (NTR gap); industry rather than firm FE; time-varying controls
